{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_1074e4b3e3e446ab9d14c2f0","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95\n4\tLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n5\t\n6\t## Why\n7\t\n8\tThe orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n9\t\n10\t`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads \"no errors\" while the caller sees rejections.\n11\t\n12\tRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n13\t\n14\t## What to do\n15\t\n16\tCall `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.\n17\t\n18\t## Acceptance criteria\n19\t\n20\t- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged\n21\t- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`\n22\t- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n23\t- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n24\t- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n25\t\n26\t## Tech notes\n27\t\n28\tKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n29\t\n30\tOut of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n31\t\n32\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1166ae26-d065-4626-9581-85325c9eeaa1","uuid":"e21c0ac7-ba7f-46a8-b27b-576aa1064139","timestamp":"2026-11-06T00:40:43.476Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4e3817ca5fe/workspace/ticket.md","content":"# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error\n\nIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95\nLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n\n## Why\n\nThe orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n\n`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads \"no errors\" while the caller sees rejections.\n\nRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n\n## What to do\n\nCall `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged\n- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`\n- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n\n## Tech notes\n\nKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n\n","numLines":32,"startLine":1,"totalLines":32}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_1074e4b3e3e446ab9d14c2f0","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_0a3d30d476d54137bbbca036","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Definition of Done\n2\t\n3\t> The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a response body rejected directly by an HTTP client — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n4\t\n5\t**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists. `createChatOrchestrator` returns an orchestrator whose `processMessage` and `processMessageStream` invoke the installed `OrchestratorHooks`. A test can drive `processMessage` with a provider that throws a string or a plain object and observe that `onError` is bypassed today because of the `error instanceof Error` gate in the `catch` block.\n6\t\n7\t## Done when these pass\n8\t\n9\t- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing** — when a turn rejects with a string (`'string boom'`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance whose `message` is `'string boom'`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n10\t      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n11\t\n12\t- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object** — when a turn rejects with a plain object (`{code: 503, detail: 'upstream down'}`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance carrying a non-empty `message`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n13\t      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n14\t\n15\t## Facets\n16\t\n17\t- [ ] In `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`, coerce a caught non-`Error` rejection to an `Error` with a readable `message` (while passing an `Error` instance through unchanged) so `hooks.onError` always fires on any rejection inside the `try` block.\n18\t- [ ] Confirm existing `Error`-instance tests in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` (`called with session and error when stream fails`, `error still propagates after onError hook`, `error path calls onError then afterSession`) remain green without modification.\n19\t- [ ] Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` describing the behaviour change for existing consumers.\n20\t\n21\t## Out of scope\n22\t\n23\t- `beforeSession` escaping the `try` block (resolved separately in HALEngine#94).\n24\t- Usage accounting across tool rounds (resolved separately in HALEngine#93).\n25\t- Widening the `onError` hook parameter type away from `Error` (the ticket keeps `(session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>`).\n26\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1166ae26-d065-4626-9581-85325c9eeaa1","uuid":"b394c646-c6b6-46a9-9d5e-a979b93b8f06","timestamp":"2026-11-06T00:40:46.211Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4e3817ca5fe/workspace/target/.lore/dod.md","content":"# Definition of Done\n\n> The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a response body rejected directly by an HTTP client — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n\n**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists. `createChatOrchestrator` returns an orchestrator whose `processMessage` and `processMessageStream` invoke the installed `OrchestratorHooks`. A test can drive `processMessage` with a provider that throws a string or a plain object and observe that `onError` is bypassed today because of the `error instanceof Error` gate in the `catch` block.\n\n## Done when these pass\n\n- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing** — when a turn rejects with a string (`'string boom'`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance whose `message` is `'string boom'`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object** — when a turn rejects with a plain object (`{code: 503, detail: 'upstream down'}`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance carrying a non-empty `message`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n\n## Facets\n\n- [ ] In `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts`, coerce a caught non-`Error` rejection to an `Error` with a readable `message` (while passing an `Error` instance through unchanged) so `hooks.onError` always fires on any rejection inside the `try` block.\n- [ ] Confirm existing `Error`-instance tests in `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` (`called with session and error when stream fails`, `error still propagates after onError hook`, `error path calls onError then afterSession`) remain green without modification.\n- [ ] Add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]` describing the behaviour change for existing consumers.\n\n## Out of scope\n\n- `beforeSession` escaping the `try` block (resolved separately in HALEngine#94).\n- Usage accounting across tool rounds (resolved separately in HALEngine#93).\n- Widening the `onError` hook parameter type away from `Error` (the ticket keeps `(session: ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>`).\n","numLines":26,"startLine":1,"totalLines":26}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_0a3d30d476d54137bbbca036","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4e3817ca5fe/home-1/.claude/skills/tdd-loop\n\nThis is the authoritative copy of Lore's TDD contract for agent runs. It is checked\ninto the Lore repo at `apps/mcp-server/agent-skills/skills/tdd-loop/` and served to\npods by the gateway's `/skills` registry.\n\nYou run the three phases yourself, in order, in one pass. Do not skip a phase and do\nnot run two facets in one round.\n\n## The three laws\n\n1. Do not write production code unless it is to make a failing test pass.\n2. Do not write more of a unit test than is sufficient to fail — a compile or import\n   failure counts.\n3. Do not write more production code than is sufficient to make the currently failing\n   test pass.\n\n## Phase 1 — RED\n\nDetect the toolchain from the project (`package.json`, `go.mod`, `pyproject.toml`,\n`Cargo.toml`, `pom.xml`, `Gemfile`, `mix.exs`, `Makefile`, CI config) and mirror the\nconventions already in the repo's tests — framework, directory, file suffix, assertion\nstyle. Assume nothing about the language.\n\n**The one-facet rule.** Name the single smallest behaviour that moves you forward. If\nthe behaviour you were handed would force more than one new facet, write the test for\nthe smallest facet only and report the leftovers rather than growing the round.\n\nWrite **exactly one** test. Run it. Confirm it fails **for the reason you expect** —\nthe behaviour is absent, not the import path typo'd or a fixture missing. A test you\ndid not run is not a red bar, it is a guess.\n\nIf a behaviour would not change the code under test at all, say so and write nothing.\nA test that forces no change is not worth writing.\n\n### No mocks, no stubs\n\nDesign every test to exercise pure logic with real values — value in, value out, not\ninteractions. A facet that seems to *require* a double is a design signal: the real\nproblem is an unmanaged side effect, not the absence of a mock. Pick a facet that is\ntestable without doubles, and note that the production code should push the I/O to the\nedges so the pure core is directly testable.\n\n- Stubbed lookup → pure function on a value. `discountFor(user)` taking a real `User`,\n  not `discountFor(userId)` fetching one behind a `UserRepository` stub.\n- Interaction mock → assert on a returned value. Have the core return the intent and\n  assert `notificationsFor(order)`; sending happens at the edge.\n- Clock/RNG stub → inject the value. `isExpired(deadline, now)`, both plain values.\n\nA true collaborator boundary that must eventually be pinned down is a separate\n**contract test**, never an ad-hoc mock sprinkled into a unit test.\n\n### Test naming\n\nThe principle is language-agnostic; the surface form follows the language.\n\n- Short, clear, scannable. The name carries the expected behaviour **and** the tested\n  data — never the implementation.\n- No \"should\".\n- Apply the *ask-why* check: a name that does not answer why the test exists is a\n  structural name, not an intent-revealing one.\n- Include the context only when the enclosing suite does not already establish it.\n\nGood: `returns 0 for an empty list`, `returns I for 1`, `throws RangeError for 0`.\nBad: `should return zero`, `test sum`, `works correctly`.\n\n## Phase 2 — GREEN\n\nWrite the fewest lines that turn the bar green. No extra features, no speculative\ngenerality, no refactoring yet.\n\n**Kent Beck's green-bar strategies:**\n\n- *Obvious implementation* — when the real code is trivial and unmistakable, write it.\n- *Fake it* — when it is not, return a constant and let a later test replace constants\n  with variables.\n- *Triangulate* — leave generalization to the NEXT test. Do not guess the general\n  solution now.\n\nRun the tests you are working against — the one you just wrote plus the acceptance\ntests that define done — by naming their files. Never the repository's whole suite:\nCI runs that on every push, and the pod's Bash hook refuses a bare `npm test` or\n`vitest run` with no path. All of what you run must pass.\n\n**Never edit the test to make it pass.** If the test is wrong, say so and stop; that is\na finding, not a green bar.\n\n### Where code goes\n\nNever create code in catch-all `utils` / `misc` / `helpers` / `common` / `shared` /\n`lib` modules. Place and name code by the domain concept it serves — discount logic in\n`pricing/`, not `utils/calc.ts`. When no home exists, create a domain-named module,\nnever a generic bucket.\n\n### Naming\n\nMeaningful but concise — one to three words (`pendingOrders`, `isContainer`,\n`retryCount`). No single letters except trivial loop indices; no `temp`/`data`/`x`; no\nsprawling four-plus-word names. Name by role: `rawInput`, `normalized`.\n\n## Phase 3 — REFACTOR\n\nThe bar is green. Improve the design without changing behaviour, and fit the new code\ninto the surrounding architecture. The suite stays green throughout.\n\n**Duplication is duplicated knowledge, not just duplicated text.** Hunt for and\ncollapse: the same business rule expressed two ways, a constant or validation\nre-derived in two places, parallel structures encoding one concept, a domain concept\nnamed differently across modules, the same idea living in both code and a test.\n\nRefactor **both** production and test code. Test refactoring counts: collapsing\nduplicated tests into one parameterized test, removing now-subsumed tests, extracting\nshared setup, clarifying names. Behaviour coverage must not shrink.\n\n### The Simple Design Dynamo\n\nReuse is a **result** of removing duplication, never a prediction. Never extract because\nsomething \"might\" be reused. For each candidate, in order:\n\n1. Remove the duplication — collapse the copies into one. The reusable shape only\n   becomes visible after the duplication is gone.\n2. Separate what varies from what stays the same.\n3. Extract a template — the algorithm steps with explicit variation points.\n4. Name each operation concretely. **If a step cannot be named, the variation is not\n   understood yet — stop and look.**\n5. Parameterize the details — lift literals into arguments. Generic logic in code,\n   specific values in data passed in.\n\nThis loops: removing duplication creates structures → you name them → better names\nraise cohesion → higher cohesion makes the next, bigger duplication visible.\n\n**Rule of three.** Two copies = notice, and remove the duplication *in place*. Promote\nto a shared module only on the third genuinely similar case. Lifting on the second copy\ncouples unrelated callers and is harder to undo than the duplication was.\n\n### Reveal intent\n\nFor any name you touch, ask \"why does this exist / what is it really?\" — the name must\nanswer that, not describe the mechanism. A function name containing \"and\"\n(`parseAndStore`) is two responsibilities; split it. Improve names iteratively:\nnonsense → structurally accurate → intent-revealing.\n\n### Fewest elements\n\nInline indirection that does not pull its weight — a wrapper that only forwards. Apply\n\"too simple to break\": never add a test for trivial composition of already-trusted\nparts. Reject premature abstraction.\n\n### Refactor discipline — this is where rounds go wrong\n\n- **Never change production code and test code in the same step.** Each step touches\n  only tests or only production code, then run the suite to green before the next.\n  Changing both at once means a green bar no longer proves the refactor was safe.\n- One target per step, always.\n- **If a step turns the suite red, revert that step** rather than chasing the failure.\n- Grep for existing abstractions to reuse before inventing new ones.\n- May move or extract code and create files, but never add behaviour or expand scope\n  beyond the current test.\n\n### Out-of-scope smells\n\nWhile you have the context loaded, note architecture and code smells you spot that are\n**unrelated** to the current round — god objects, leaky abstractions, missing seams,\ndead code. **Do not fix them**; that blows the round's scope. Collect them as\n`future_improvements`: location + smell + one-line suggested fix. Report them; act on\nnone.\n\n## Ending the round\n\nCommit and push per the delivery contract in your task instructions — in a pod, the\nwork dies with the container otherwise. Commit only on green; a red suite is never\npushed.\n\nReport: the facet you closed, the facet you would take next, the post-refactor test\nresult, and the `future_improvements` list.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1166ae26-d065-4626-9581-85325c9eeaa1","uuid":"04e79330-693e-492c-ab21-dd3fb33600bf","timestamp":"2026-11-06T00:40:49.676Z","isSynthetic":true}

ChatSession, error: Error) => Promise<void>;\n  /** The supported seam for an EU AI Act Art. 14 human-oversight control: fires before each known tool's executor, and a returned ToolResponse replaces the call (see docs/adding-a-tool.md); it receives the model's raw tool input and, through session, the caller's authHeaders, so a policy that logs either logs personal data and credential material; the engine asserts nothing about any policy installed here. */\n  beforeToolCall?: (session: ChatSession, call: ToolCall) => Promise<ToolResponse | undefined>;\n  /** Fires when the model asks for a tool round the budget refuses, after the last provider call and before afterModelResponse; a returned string reaches the user as the turn's closing text, and the engine writes none of its own (see specs/hal-engine-tool-budget/spec.md). */\n  onToolBudgetExhausted?: (session: ChatSession, budget: ToolBudgetInfo) => Promise<string | undefined>;\n}\n\nexport interface ToolBudgetInfo {\n  maxToolRounds: number;\n  requestedTools: string[];\n}\n\ntype BeforeToolCall = NonNullable<OrchestratorHooks['beforeToolCall']>;\ntype OnToolBudgetExhausted = NonNullable<OrchestratorHooks['onToolBudgetExhausted']>;\n\nexport const TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED = 'tool_budget_exhausted';\n\nexport interface ChatOrchestrator {\n  processMessage(session: ChatSession): Promise<string>;\n  processMessageStream(session: ChatSession): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk>;\n}\n\nexport interface ChatOrchestratorOptions {\n  maxToolRounds?: number;\n  contextConfig?: Partial<ContextConfig>;\n  promptBuilderOptions?: PromptBuilderOptions;\n  hooks?: OrchestratorHooks;\n  sessionStore?: SessionStore;\n}\n\ninterface ToolExecutionResult {\n  clientMessages: OutgoingMessage[];\n  suppressOutput: boolean;\n}\nexport function createChatOrchestrator(\n  provider: AIProvider,\n  promptBuilder: PromptBuilder,\n  toolRegistry?: ToolRegistry,\n  options?: ChatOrchestratorOptions\n): ChatOrchestrator {\n  const maxToolRounds = normalizeToolRounds(options?.maxToolRounds);\n  const contextConfig = createContextConfig(options?.contextConfig);\n  const toolInstructions = toolRegistry?.getPromptInstructions();\n  const baseSystemPrompt = promptBuilder.build({...options?.promptBuilderOptions, toolInstructions});\n  const tools = toolRegistry?.getDefinitions();\n  const hooks = options?.hooks;\n  const sessionStore = options?.sessionStore;\n\n  return {\n    async processMessage(session: ChatSession): Promise<string> {\n      return collectText(this.processMessageStream(session));\n    },\n\n    async *processMessageStream(session: ChatSession): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n      try {\n        if (hooks?.beforeSession) await hooks.beforeSession(session);\n\n        let userMessage = lastUserContent(session);\n\n        if (hooks?.beforeUserInput) {\n          userMessage = await rewriteUserMessage(session, userMessage, hooks.beforeUserInput);\n        }\n\n        if (hooks?.afterUserInput) await hooks.afterUserInput(session, userMessage);\n\n        const systemPrompt = hooks?.beforeModelResponse\n          ? await hooks.beforeModelResponse(session, baseSystemPrompt)\n          : baseSystemPrompt;\n\n        const messages: Message[] = toMessages(session.entries, contextConfig);\n        let totalUsage: UsageMetadata | undefined;\n        let responseText = '';\n\n        // Bounded by the budget gate below, not the header: maxToolRounds executed rounds, maxToolRounds + 1 provider calls.\n        for (let round = 0; ; round++) {\n          log.info('orchestrator', 'starting round', {round});\n          const pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[] = [];\n\n          const outcome = yield* streamRound(provider, {messages, systemPrompt, tools}, pendingToolCalls);\n          responseText += outcome.text;\n          totalUsage = accumulateUsage(totalUsage, outcome.usage);\n\n          if (!shouldContinueToolLoop(outcome.stopReason, pendingToolCalls, toolRegistry)) break;\n          if (budgetSpent(round, maxToolRounds, pendingToolCalls)) {\n            const budget = {maxToolRounds, requestedTools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name)};\n            responseText += yield* closeExhaustedTurn(session, budget, hooks?.onToolBudgetExhausted);\n            break;\n          }\n\n          log.info('orchestrator', 'executing tools', {tools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name)});\n          const {clientMessages, suppressOutput} = await executeToolCalls(\n            pendingToolCalls,\n            messages,\n            session,\n            toolCallRunner(toolRegistry!, session, hooks?.beforeToolCall)\n          );\n          log.info('orchestrator', 'tool execution complete', {\n            clientMessageCount: clientMessages.length,\n            clientMessageTypes: clientMessages.map(m => m.type),\n            suppressOutput,\n          });\n\n          if (clientMessages.length > 0) {\n            yield {type: 'tool_result' as const, clientMessages};\n          }\n\n          if (suppressOutput) {\n            yield {type: 'suppress_output' as const};\n          }\n        }\n\n        if (hooks?.afterModelResponse) await hooks.afterModelResponse(session, responseText, totalUsage);\n      } catch (error) {\n        if (hooks?.onError && error instanceof Error) {\n          await hooks.onError(session, error);\n        }\n        throw error;\n      } finally {\n        // Before both: a provider that threw mid-stream leaves an entry open, and nothing should persist it that way.\n        commitStreamingEntries(session);\n        try {\n          if (hooks?.afterSession) await hooks.afterSession(session);\n        } finally {\n          await saveSession(sessionStore, session);\n        }\n      }\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n// A negative budget means no tool rounds; a non-finite one, NaN included, falls back to the default rather than never ending.\nfunction normalizeToolRounds(value: number | undefined): number {\n  if (value === undefined || !Number.isFinite(value)) return DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS;\n  return Math.max(0, Math.floor(value));\n}\n\n// Gates execution, not the provider call: a round nobody can read is never run, and the call that read the last one already has.\nfunction budgetSpent(round: number, maxToolRounds: number, pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]): boolean {\n  if (round < maxToolRounds) return false;\n  log.warn('orchestrator', 'tool budget exhausted', {\n    maxToolRounds,\n    requestedTools: pendingToolCalls.map(tc => tc.name),\n  });\n  return true;\n}\n\n// The stop always follows the text: the round's own stop already committed its entry, and a bare text chunk would open one never committed.\nasync function* closeExhaustedTurn(\n  session: ChatSession,\n  budget: ToolBudgetInfo,\n  hook?: OnToolBudgetExhausted\n): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, string> {\n  const sentence = (hook ? await hook(session, budget) : undefined) ?? '';\n  if (sentence !== '') yield {type: 'text', text: sentence};\n  yield {type: 'stop', stopReason: TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED};\n  return sentence;\n}\n\ninterface RoundOutcome {\n  stopReason: string;\n  text: string;\n  usage?: UsageMetadata;\n}\n\n// `yield*` in the caller evaluates to this return, so the round's totals come back as data.\nasync function* streamRound(\n  provider: AIProvider,\n  request: SendMessageParams,\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[]\n): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk, RoundOutcome> {\n  let stopReason = '';\n  let text = '';\n  let usage: UsageMetadata | undefined;\n\n  for await (const chunk of provider.sendMessage(request)) {\n    yield chunk;\n    collectToolCalls(chunk, pendingToolCalls);\n    stopReason = extractStopReason(chunk) ?? stopReason;\n    usage = extractUsage(chunk) ?? usage;\n    if (chunk.type === 'text') text += chunk.text;\n  }\n\n  return {stopReason, text, usage};\n}\n\n// A changed message is also written back to the session's last user entry.\nasync function rewriteUserMessage(\n  session: ChatSession,\n  userMessage: string,\n  hook: (session: ChatSession, userMessage: string) => Promise<string>\n): Promise<string> {\n  const modified = await hook(session, userMessage);\n  if (modified === userMessage) return userMessage;\n\n  updateLastUserContent(session, modified);\n  return modified;\n}\n\nfunction lastUserContent(session: ChatSession): string {\n  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const entry = session.entries[i];\n    if (entry.role === 'user') return entry.content;\n  }\n  return '';\n}\n\nfunction updateLastUserContent(session: ChatSession, content: string): void {\n  for (let i = session.entries.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const entry = session.entries[i];\n    if (entry.role === 'user') {\n      entry.content = content;\n      return;\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// One runner per round: the policy sees each known call before its executor, and an unknown name keeps the registry's own path.\nfunction toolCallRunner(toolRegistry: ToolRegistry, session: ChatSession, beforeToolCall?: BeforeToolCall) {\n  const context: ToolContext = {\n    userId: session.userId,\n    sessionId: session.sessionId,\n    workspaceId: session.workspaceId,\n    authHeaders: session.authHeaders,\n  };\n\n  return async (tc: ToolCall): Promise<ToolResponse> => {\n    const declined =\n      beforeToolCall && toolRegistry.has(tc.name) ? await consultPolicy(beforeToolCall, session, tc) : undefined;\n    return declined ?? toolRegistry.execute(tc.name, tc.input, context);\n  };\n}\n\n// A throwing policy declines its call rather than failing the turn: every tool_use must still be answered.\nasync function consultPolicy(\n  policy: BeforeToolCall,\n  session: ChatSession,\n  tc: ToolCall\n): Promise<ToolResponse | undefined> {\n  try {\n    return await policy(session, tc);\n  } catch (error) {\n    log.warn('orchestrator', 'beforeToolCall threw, so the call is declined', {\n      tool: tc.name,\n      errorType: error instanceof Error ? error.name : typeof error,\n    });\n    return {result: `The ${tc.name} call was declined and not performed.`};\n  }\n}\n\nasync function executeToolCalls(\n  pendingToolCalls: ToolCall[],\n  messages: Message[],\n  session: ChatSession,\n  runToolCall: (tc: ToolCall) => Promise<ToolResponse>\n): Promise<ToolExecutionResult> {\n  messages.push(buildToolCallMessages(pendingToolCalls));\n\n  const responses = await Promise.all(\n    pendingToolCalls.map(async tc => {\n      const response = await runToolCall(tc);\n      return {tc, response};\n    })\n  );\n\n  const toolResults: ToolResultContent[] = responses.map(({tc, response}) => ({\n    type: 'tool_result' as const,\n    toolUseId: tc.id,\n    content: response.result,\n  }));\n  messages.push({role: 'user', content: toolResults});\n\n  const rawClientMessages = responses.flatMap(({response}) => response.clientMessages ?? []);\n\n  return {\n    clientMessages: assignEntryIndices(rawClientMessages, session),\n    suppressOutput: responses.some(({response}) => response.suppressAssistantResponse === true),\n  };\n}\n\nfunction assignEntryIndices(clientMessages: OutgoingMessage[], session: ChatSession): OutgoingMessage[] {\n  return clientMessages.map(msg => {\n    if (msg.type !== 'entry_upsert') return msg;\n    const index = appendEntry(session, msg.entry);\n    return {...msg, index};\n  });\n}\n\n// Adds per-round token counts so the hook receives the total across all provider calls in the turn.\nfunction accumulateUsage(acc: UsageMetadata | undefined, next: UsageMetadata | undefined): UsageMetadata | undefined {\n  if (!acc) return next;\n  if (!next) return acc;\n  return {\n    inputTokens: acc.inputTokens + next.inputTokens,\n    outputTokens: acc.outputTokens + next.outputTokens,\n    totalTokens: acc.totalTokens + next.totalTokens,\n  };\n}\n\n// A store outage is not a reason to fail the turn the customer already received.\nasync function saveSession(store: SessionStore | undefined, session: ChatSession): Promise<void> {\n  if (!store?.save) return;\n\n  try {\n    await store.save(session);\n  } catch (error) {\n    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);\n    log.error('orchestrator', 'session save failed', {sessionId: session.sessionId, error: message});\n  }\n}\n","numLines":346,"startLine":1,"totalLines":346}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_bc6316cfec61417b9de3a46b","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_6ebb865144b14aa09d47adbc","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n2\t\n3\t| Field  | Value                |\n4\t| ------ | -------------------- |\n5\t| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n6\t| Status | Shipped              |\n7\t\n8\t`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n9\t\n10\t## Installing hooks through config\n11\t\n12\t- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n13\t- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n14\t- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).\n15\t- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n16\t- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).\n17\t- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n18\t- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).\n19\t- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).\n20\t\n21\t## Engine startup\n22\t\n23\t- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).\n24\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1166ae26-d065-4626-9581-85325c9eeaa1","uuid":"5dfaddff-ac95-4375-b63f-2ee0054a0b0f","timestamp":"2026-11-06T00:40:59.914Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/d4e3817ca5fe/workspace/target/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md","content":"# Config-Installed Orchestrator Hooks\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#36 |\n| Status | Shipped              |\n\n`OrchestratorHooks` is the engine's only lifecycle seam, and `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` is the supported way to install it: `createHalEngine` forwards the set to `createChatOrchestrator`, so a hook a deployer passes through the factory reaches the running orchestrator rather than sitting unread on the config object. This spec pins that forwarding and the measured semantics the seam already carries, so the hook-based features that follow in this epic — transparency disclosure, audit and usage recording, human oversight, provider failover — specify against real behaviour rather than against what the hook names suggest.\n\n## Installing hooks through config\n\n- A hook passed through `orchestrator.hooks` is forwarded to the orchestrator and fires ([validated by: forwards an orchestrator hook, so one passed through the config actually fires](../../src/config.test.ts#L19)).\n- An engine built with no `orchestrator` key at all still processes a message, so the field is optional in fact and not only in the type ([validated by: processes a message when the config declares no orchestrator key at all](../../src/config.test.ts#L95)).\n- A `beforeModelResponse` hook installed through config is handed the base system prompt built from `prompt`, proving the hook reaches the orchestrator and is wired into the prompt pipeline rather than only being stored on the config ([validated by: hands a config-installed beforeModelResponse hook the built base system prompt, not merely storing it](../../src/config.test.ts#L129)).\n- The value the hook returns then replaces the system prompt the provider receives; this is exercised at the orchestrator layer because `HalEngineConfig.provider` takes a `ProviderConfig` and offers no seam to inject a recording provider through config ([validated by: replaces system prompt with returned value](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L221)).\n- For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).\n- A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n- `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).\n- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).\n\n## Engine startup\n\n- The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).\n","numLines":24,"startLine":1,"totalLines":24}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_6ebb865144b14aa09d47adbc","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_74785e61170645bf83607777","type":"tool_result","content":"commit 64143f70d171548198336e81e6c5a2cee685d35f\nAuthor: loop-bench <loop-bench@localhost>\nDate:   Tue Oct 20 11:31:37 2026 +0200\n\n    test(orchestrator): pin onError on non-Error rejection\n\ndiff --git a/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md b/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md\nindex 66ff9d3..7b773cf 100644\n--- a/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md\n+++ b/specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md\n@@ -16,13 +16,8 @@\n - For a session that completes without error the hooks fire in the order `beforeSession` → `beforeUserInput` → `afterUserInput` → `beforeModelResponse` → `afterModelResponse` → `afterSession` ([validated by: fires the lifecycle hooks in documented order for a session that completes without error](../../src/config.test.ts#L153)).\n - A `beforeSession` that throws reaches the caller as a rejection, and also runs `onError` with the thrown error and then `afterSession`, because the call sits inside the same `try`/`finally` as the rest of the turn. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n - `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).\n+- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).\n \n ## Engine startup\n \n - The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).\n-\n-## Measured semantics — out of scope\n-\n-This property of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` is recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue does not change it; that is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.\n-\n-- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n# Lore test-command interface (lore_list_tests / lore_run_test).\n# Written for this repo's Jest suite rather than adapted from the Vitest\n# equivalent for a Vitest suite: the report shapes happen to match, but the\n# invocations do not.\n- id: hal-engine-jest\n  name: HAL Engine Jest suite\n  cwd: .\n  description: >-\n    The ts-jest unit suite over src/ and scripts/ (jest.config.js roots), run\n    on every pull request in .github/workflows/ci.yml as the \"Test\" step.\n    Selectors are \"<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>\" as emitted by the\n    list command. An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n - `afterModelResponse` is called once per user message after the round loop exits and is passed `totalUsage` — the sum of the usage every provider call in the turn reported, not the last round alone ([validated by: sums the usage of every round, not only the last](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L555)).\n+- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` when a string or object is thrown — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L52), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L63)).\n \n ## Engine startup\n \n - The engine's `start()` method rejects the returned promise when it cannot bind the configured port, rather than emitting an unhandled error event that would take the process down ([validated by: rejects instead of taking the process down with an unhandled error event](../../src/config.test.ts#L195)).\n-\n-## Measured semantics — out of scope\n-\n-This property of `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` is recorded so the hook features that follow specify against real behaviour. This issue does not change it; that is a separate, out-of-scope change owned by no issue in this epic.\n-\n-- The `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error` ([chatOrchestrator.ts#L150](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts#L150)), so a rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string or object — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n# Lore test-command interface (lore_list_tests / lore_run_test).\n# Written for this repo's Jest suite rather than adapted from the Vitest\n# equivalent for a Vitest suite: the report shapes happen to match, but the\n# invocations do not.\n- id: hal-engine-jest\n  name: HAL Engine Jest suite\n  cwd: .\n  description: >-\n    The ts-jest unit suite over src/ and scripts/ (jest.config.js roots), run\n    on every pull request in .github/workflows/ci.yml as the \"Test\" step.\n    Selectors are \"<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>\" as emitted by the\n    list command.
